atlas · how it works

Write it once. Every agent works from it.

Your team keeps what it agrees on in Atlas. Agents read it over MCP, and anything they want to change comes back to a person as a change request.

The loop in four steps.

  1. Write it down. Your team keeps skills, pages and metric definitions in Atlas, in a live editor with comments and history.
  2. Connect your agents. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or your own agent connects over MCP and signs in as a person.
  3. Agents read. An agent searches and reads what its person can open, and answers from the same copy as every other agent.
  4. People approve changes. When an agent wants to fix something, it opens a change request, and a person approves the diff.

Three kinds of context. Each kept once.

Skills

How a job is done here. Written procedures that agents follow, like the month-end close or the deploy runbook. Each save is a new version with a note on what changed.

Knowledge

What is true here. Pages your team writes together, with comments, tasks and links between pages. Agents read the same pages people do.

Metrics

What a word means here. A metric is SQL over your BigQuery or Snowflake warehouse, agreed once, so every agent gives the same number for churn.

How it stays right over time.

Versions

Nothing is overwritten. Open any earlier version, compare it, and restore it as a new one. Deleted pages go to a trash you can restore from.

Change requests

An agent's edit arrives as a diff, like a pull request. A person approves or rejects it, block by block.

Workflows

Scheduled jobs run a model you connect, read your sources and propose updates, so context stays current without anyone chasing it.

Access

Pages and skills sit in a teamspace or a private space. The browser, the API and MCP use the same rules, so an agent sees what its person sees.

Under the hood.

  • One endpoint

    Every agent connects to the same MCP endpoint and gets tools to search, read, run warehouse queries and propose changes.

  • Your warehouse stays read-only

    Warehouse queries only read, and each returns a bounded number of rows.

  • Your model, your key

    Atlas calls a model only when a workflow you set up runs, with the provider and key you connect.

  • We run it for you

    Ensemble Labs hosts Atlas on Fly.io in Paris. Each company is its own workspace, and access is invitation-only.

Start with one team.
